questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer: Language development, improve my German while studying.

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: A German speaking destination.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Humbolt zu Berlin Universität, or more specific the psychological faculty, did not offer the sufficient support needed for an exchange student.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The general exchange office of Humbolt Universität made it easy before the exchange.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There were general info days which provided some assistance. When it came to the psychological department, I received no assistance whatsoever. The Erasmus student workers where not able to help me with any of my questions, and I felt very on my own. No information provided on what to do when I didn't receive the Course I needed. I had to have a lot of random communication with the professors on my own. No special assistance for exchange students, they are left all on their own, and expected to know everything and be able to do everything just like the regular students. All in all, it made my stay stressful and confusing.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Not sufficient help.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found it through friends.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The campus of Humbolt Universität, the psychological department, is very far away from the city center, so it would have been very boring to live on campus. This cannot be recommended, as Adlershof (where the Psychological Institute is) is a very horrible and grey place.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They cannot help students with housing.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Very confusing online registration, you have to be fast, there is not enough places.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: A few info zoom meetings where instructions were given.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very, cause then found out that all exchange students will get a spot no matter what. But this was not communicated.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just go with the flow, trust the very confusing process. Just show up to the courses you don't get and say you are Erasmus.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The academic programme is a bit conservative but also interesting to experience as a Dane.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Level was fine, definitely a challenge in German, but can be managed.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very conservative.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Entwicklungspsychologie 
Psychologie und Gesellschaft (Entwicklungspsychologie 1+2)
Arbeits-, Ingenieur, und Organisationspsychologie
Angewandte Methoden und Interventionen der Arbeits-, Ingenieur- & Organisationspsychologie
Grundlagen von Medizin und Pharmakologie

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Do as many seminars (like Psychologie und Gesellschaft) as possible. No exams, only one presentation. 

Grundlagen von Medizin und Pharmakologie has a very cool professor, and I enjoyed the course a lot, even though it was a hard exam.

questions.answer: Housing is not that cheap in Berlin anymore.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: did not attend any

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: some sport activities, but you have to be very fast as the spots are gone in 1 minute. I did not make it.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I think some of the sport programs are really nice and they are cheap

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: dancing, eating, swimming in the lakes, vintage shopping, drinking good German beer:)

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: just sit down and chat with people at the lectures

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: none

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: the club culture:)

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. It is a very confusing system at HU compared to UCPH, and there is not a lot of help offered, but it will somehow work out in the end.
2. Try to find a housing with Germans, and get out of the Erasmus bobble. Download the app
WG-gesucht.de
3. there is a lot of nice opportunities to enjoy life with cheap restaurants and some of the best clubs in Europe if you enjoy Techno.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Maybe try to get some courses in Mitte (language courses etc.) and not only Psychology, so that you won't be spending 2hours everyday in public transportation.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
My German improved. 
I had a nice semester in a lovely city. 
I enjoyed the "Medizin & Pharmakologie" course so much, and this is not available in UCPH, so I highly recommend.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: That HU psychology doesn't care much for Erasmus students, and we are left on our own.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
